next_steps: Redwood to run 1k-query benchmark matrix across shortlisted models (quant/float) by 2025-10-14
Customer to share 200 labeled dev examples and key PII redaction rules by 2025-10-10
Schedule follow-up to review bench results and pick final model for week of 2025-10-20
action_items: Samir: send benchmark spreadsheet and access instructions (due 2025-10-08)
Nina: set up test endpoints on Redwood sandbox for Acadia (due 2025-10-09)
Mikhail: share sample workload trace and expected QPS profile (due 2025-10-10)
Priya: define success metrics (F1 for extraction, latency p95 target) and share by 2025-10-10
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-07 16:00 PT · Duration: ~52m · Recording: enabled
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Gomez (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Acadia CTO), Mikhail Orlov (ML Lead), Priya Singh (Product), Daniel Park (SRE)
Shared: deck 'Acadia POC scoping v3' (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link)

[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Samir, AE for Redwood, Nina and Jordan are our engineers, and we heard from Priya that you want to pick a model for a focused POC for your multi-domain extraction workload, is that right?
[00:19] Laura (Acadia): yeah thanks, Samir. we want something open-model-first if poss — cost matters and we need on-prem later possibly, plus strong english + french + spanish support. also heavy domain terms for financial regs.
[00:34] Nina (Redwood): great. quick clarification on success criteria — do you have a hard latency SLA? or is quality primary?
[00:42] Priya (Acadia): quality is primary but latency matters for live workflows. goal is p95 < 350ms for single-turn extraction on a 1-3 sentence input. throughput target is around 40-60 QPS for the peak path. cost target — we'd like to keep inference spend < $0.20 per 1k tokens-ish if possible, but we know that's tricky with large 70B models.
[01:05] Mikhail (Acadia): and from ML side we care about our extraction F1 — baseline is 0.87 on our tuned DistilBERT pipeline. we want to beat that on most entities but maintain stability.
[01:18] Jordan (Redwood): perfect. that gives us three axis: quality (F1), latency (p95), and cost. we'll propose a shortlist with tradeoffs.

--- Topics / Quick agenda: Model shortlist, bench plan, workload sizing, success criteria, timeline ---

[02:02] Samir (Redwood): ok model shortlist we propose to bench initially — note these are open/open-ish models and variants: 1) Mistral-Instruct-7B (quant 4/8 bit), 2) Llama-2-70B-chat (int8/qat variants), 3) Falcon-40B-Instruct, 4) MPT-7B-Instruct / MPT-7B-Chat, 5) RedPajama-INCITE-70B-instruct (as a heavy quality anchor). we'll also include a compact multilingual candidate like BLOOMZ-7B-mt or XLM-based tuned variant for French/Spanish edge-cases.
[02:33] Laura (Acadia): got it. curious why include both 7B and 70B — interested in the quality vs cost tradeoff.
[02:42] Nina (Redwood): exactly — smaller models (7B family) often give good latency and cheap quantized costs, may hit your throughput/latency targets easily, but can lose domain-specific terminologies. 70B class tends to be more robust on uncommon tokens but costs more and needs bigger GPU (A100/H100) to meet low-latency unless heavily quantized and kernel-optimized.
[03:05] Mikhail (Acadia): any thoughts on instruction-tuning vs fine-tuning? we have 2k labeled examples and can do LoRA if needed.
[03:14] Nina (Redwood): for your extraction task, a LoRA/few-shot prompt plus lightweight instruction-tuning on a 7B could close a lot of the gap. we recommend starting with the smallest viable model in the shortlist and then iterate. for the POC we'll bench both out-of-the-box instr-tuned checkpoints and a quick LoRA on 2k samples.

[04:00] Samir (Redwood): benchmark plan — we'll run a 1k-query benchmark matrix across the shortlist: metrics captured — exact-match/F1 for entities, latency p50/p95, tokens per call, throughput at batch sizes 1/4/8, and memory footprint. we'll run float16 and quantized (8-bit and 4-bit where supported).
[04:25] Priya (Acadia): do you replicate our preproc? we have a tokenization shim and custom redaction rules.
[04:31] Jordan (Redwood): yes, we can drop in your preproc and use your trace for realistic lengths. Mikhail, please share ~200 dev examples and a sample trace for sequence length distribution, that will make the bench realistic.
[04:44] Mikhail (Acadia): will do. small note — many of our examples hit 512 tokens because they append metadata and logs.

[05:05] Daniel (Acadia): on infra, we will likely start hosted + dedicated later. any constraints for on-prem? we run Kubernetes with Nvidia A100 nodes.
[05:15] Nina (Redwood): that's perfect — Redwood Private supports your on-prem A100s and we can deploy the same model variant. note: 70B on single A100 will limit batch size; for <350ms p95 you may need multi-GPU or H100s unless we quantize and use specialized kernels.

[06:00] Samir (Redwood): quick quality note — multilingual edge cases: BLOOMZ or XLM variants will usually do better on zero-shot Spanish/French. Mistral and Falcon have decent multilingual capability but less so on low-resource phrases in regulatory Spanish. hence the plan to include a multilingual 7B candidate.

[06:28] Laura (Acadia): ok tradeoffs seem clear. another requirement — redaction & PII: we cannot send raw text of certain fields to hosted services until legal signs off. is there a way to run partial masking?
[06:42] Jordan (Redwood): yes we can run a two-stage flow: local pre-mask (on-prem) then hosted for model inference on masked data, or run the whole thing in Redwood Private. we'll note that for the POC we'll simulate both approaches and flag any score drift from masked inputs.

[07:15] Mikhail (Acadia): bench envs — can Redwood provide both an A100-backed sandbox and a lower-cost GPU (T4-like) to see cost/latency slope?
[07:24] Nina (Redwood): yes — we'll run on A100 and a T4-equivalent to illustrate latency/cost tradeoffs. T4 will show very different numbers especially for 70B.

[08:00] Samir (Redwood): timeline proposal: kickoff bench this week, initial results in 6 business days, follow-up to decide model week of Oct 20, then a 4-week POC to measure end-to-end metrics with LoRA & redaction flows. does that timeline work?
[08:15] Priya (Acadia): yes that fits our fiscal needs.

[08:35] (Transcript noise) Speaker labelled as Speaker 3: uh-huh, mm hmm — small crosstalk

[09:00] Nina (Redwood): technical bench specifics — for each model we'll record: model size, quantization mode, GPU type, batch size, KV cache behavior for multi-turn (we'll simulate short prompts and single-turn extraction), and cost estimate per 1k tokens based on Redwood pricing assumptions.
[09:25] Mikhail (Acadia): can you include memory headroom numbers? our SRE needs to know temp disk + mem usage to plan pods.
[09:31] Jordan (Redwood): yes we'll include peak GPU memory and recommended node sizes.

[10:00] Laura (Acadia): about evaluation — we want entity extraction F1 but also regression checks for hallucination (precision penalties). how do you capture hallucination?
[10:12] Nina (Redwood): we'll include precision and false positive rates and a hallucination score for open-answer fields by comparing to reference and an extra manual spot-check sample. we can also run a small human eval on 100 random responses if you want higher confidence.

[11:00] Priya (Acadia): curious about quantization accuracy — is 4-bit going to kill precision for legal terms?
[11:07] Nina (Redwood): sometimes 4-bit can degrade rare token handling; we will show that in the bench. our approach: use 8-bit quant where you need token fidelity, reserve 4-bit for heavy throughput paths after QA.

[12:00] Samir (Redwood): modeling plan recap — bench this shortlist: Mistral-7B, MPT-7B, BLOOMZ-7B-mt (multilingual), Falcon-40B-instruct, Llama-2-70B-chat, RedPajama-70B anchor. we'll run LoRA experiments on the top 2-3 performers by F1.

[13:00] Mikhail (Acadia): perfect. also want to see prompt vs LoRA delta — how much lift we're getting.

[14:00] Daniel (Acadia): SRE question — tokenization parity: we use a slightly modified BPE that collapses certain hyphenation. could that change token counts materially?
[14:14] Jordan (Redwood): tokenization differences change costs and latencies; we'll run with your tokenizer shim so the bench uses exact token counts.

[15:00] (Minor filler, laughter)

[15:30] Nina (Redwood): sample bench cases — 1) short single sentence extraction (avg 32 tokens), 2) medium multi-sentence with metadata (avg 220 tokens), 3) long appended logs (avg 520 tokens). these correspond to your trace buckets.

[16:00] Priya (Acadia): on success metrics — define pass/fail for POC: improvement >0.02 F1 over baseline AND latency p95 below 350ms on chosen infra OR cost-per-1k-tokens improvement over our current hosted vendor by >25% while holding quality within 0.01 F1. We have two acceptable success paths: quality-first or cost-first.

[16:35] Samir (Redwood): we'll codify those into the bench spreadsheet as gates.

[17:15] Mikhail (Acadia): any redwood-specific knobs we should consider? batching, prefix cache?
[17:21] Nina (Redwood): yes, Redwood runtime supports KV/prefix caching, continuous batching and route policies. for your workload, prefix caching helps if many queries reuse common prologs (templates). we will measure prefix hit rates with your trace and show cost savings.

[18:00] Laura (Acadia): security/compliance — we need SOC2 + SSO (SAML) + audit logs. what's included in POC?
[18:10] Samir (Redwood): Redwood hosted has SOC2, and Redwood Private gives you audit logs and SSO integration. for the POC we'll enable audit logging on the sandbox and provide SAML test connector if you want. we'll share security docs after this call.

[19:00] Priya (Acadia): legal wants to see data residency options — our European customers require EU-only processing.
[19:08] Jordan (Redwood): we can run region pinned clusters for EU; again we'll document that in the security packet and include it in follow-up.

[20:00] (Noise, small overlap)

[21:00] Samir (Redwood): pricing preview — rough cost estimates: MPT/Mistral 7B quantized on A100 -> low cost per 1k tokens; Falcon-40B mid; 70B class notably higher unless very aggressive quant. we'll include concrete numbers in bench doc. these are estimates only.

[22:00] Mikhail (Acadia): please itemize infra costs vs Redwood managed fees so we can present to finance.

[23:00] Nina (Redwood): will do — spreadsheet will have per-GPU per-hour cost, estimated tokens/day, and Redwood service fees line items.

[24:00] Laura (Acadia): can we get a quick demo of the sandbox after the bench? like an interactive notebook?

[24:08] Samir (Redwood): yes, after we run the bench we'll provision sandbox endpoints and an example notebook for your engineers to run experiments.

[25:00] (Cross talk)

[26:00] Priya (Acadia): one more — model lineage and rollback: if we roll out, we want to pin versions and do canaries. is that supported?
[26:08] Jordan (Redwood): yes Redwood rollouts, canary flags and automatic fallback are supported; we'll show a sample canary plan for production.

[27:00] Samir (Redwood): ok quick risks: 1) tokenization mismatch, 2) 70B latency/cost, 3) PII/contractual restrictions. we'll mitigate with your tokenizer, focus on 7B fast-paths, and provide Private option for redacted flows.

[28:00] Mikhail (Acadia): good.

[29:00] (Short silence, typing)

[30:00] Samir (Redwood): recap & next steps — (1) Acadia shares 200 dev examples + tokenization shim + workload trace by 2025-10-10, (2) Redwood runs 1k-query bench matrix across shortlist with float16/8-bit/4-bit where possible and both A100 + T4-equivalent, deliver results by 2025-10-14, (3) follow-up call week of 2025-10-20 to review and pick model for LoRA/4-week POC.

[30:30] Priya (Acadia): agreed. also please include redaction simulation results.
[30:38] Samir (Redwood): noted.

[31:00] Laura (Acadia): thanks — appreciate the clarity. one ask — someone on Redwood can join our platform review call next week?

[31:12] Samir (Redwood): yes Jordan or Nina can join. we'll pick a time after the bench kickoff.

[31:45] (Wrap) Samir: ok closing — we'll send the benchmark sheet and access instructions after the call. thanks everyone.

[32:00] (End of recording)

Notes: occasional transcription errors present (named entities sometimes miscaptured), speaker attribution may be slightly off for short interjections.
